citacoes.trecho: We compare five prompt strategies: Baseline; Time-Opt (targeting O(1)/O(log n)); Pythonic (encouraging idioms/builtins); Zero-Verbosity (raw code only); and CoT (step-by-step reasoning).
We evaluate Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct [5] (T=0.2, float16) on 257 MBPP sanitized tasks, each requiring at least two passing assert cases.
Dynamically, solutions execute in an isolated multiprocessing.Process (2s timeout), where the Correctness Rate is defined by the proportion of passed assertions.
Statically, we analyze maintainability via Cyclomatic Complexity (CC) [6] and code length (LOC), and algorithm efficiency via AST-based loop depth.
Evaluation uses bootstrap CIs (n=1,000) to account for sampling uncertainty.
We term this prompt-bias: a prompt-induced deviation whereby the model sacrifices correctness or maintainability in exchange for superficial compliance with the directive.
Zero-Verbosity’s −40% relative drop stems from a 34% syntax-error rate.

At max_new_tokens=512, the reasoning chain consumes tokens otherwise allocated to the function body, resulting in truncated implementations—consistent with CoT scaling findings [4] that reasoning scaffolds benefit larger models disproportionately.
To validate this, we measured mean output token length: CoT used 489±28 tokens on average versus 213±61 for Baseline, confirming near-constant token-budget exhaustion.
Practitioners seeking concise output should use post-processing filters rather than structural truncation.

Pythonic produces the tightest CC distribution (mean 2.76, LOC 10.15), while Zero-Verbosity is the pronounced outlier (CC max = 54, LOC 19.75), indicating that the model generates convoluted control flows to compensate for absent structural context.

Time-Opt shows approximately the same CC as Baseline, suggesting that 8B-scale models respond to time-optimization directives not by restructuring algorithmic logic but by adding shallow heuristics—dictionary lookups, early-exit conditions—that increase branch count without improving asymptotic complexity: optimization theater.
CoT consistently elevates CC (mean > 4.0 for all models), confirming that reasoning chains produce structurally more complex code without corresponding correctness gains at this scale.
Mistral-7B does not benefit from Pythonic prompting in correctness (0.37), suggesting model-specific sensitivity to idiomatic framing that warrants further investigation.
Limitations include single-pass evaluation per condition (mitigated by bootstrap CIs), restriction to short algorithmic MBPP tasks, and open questions about frontier-model generalization.
(3) Reserve CoT for larger models: at 8B scale, token-budget exhaustion truncates function bodies and reduces correctness.
